A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TabletopGen and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Despite v4's changed title and expanded robotics focus, the core method and retained experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-generation comparisons, DRO/TSA ablations, a user study with 126 valid questionnaires, runtime measurements, and qualitative reconstruction and manipulation demonstrations.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark, ablation, and user-study results and adds text-generation comparisons, physical-stability measurements, viewpoint analyses, and simulated and real-robot policy results.

M1.justification: The instance reconstruction, canonicalization, DRO losses, and TSA anchor selection and scaling remain unchanged. v4 extends the proposed simulation workflow with LLM-based task generation, motion planning, and multimodal trajectory collection (Section 3.3). This is a downstream extension of a framework that already supported simulated manipulation in v1; regrouping four stages into three does not itself change the algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 adds policy learning and physical-robot deployment for mango placement, strawberry placement, and block stacking, plus a separate trajectory-replay demonstration. These extend v1's simulated manipulation scenarios into real-world transfer. Real-photo reconstruction already existed in v1, while its dedicated cartoon-input reconstruction example is omitted.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated Holodeck-table to the text-driven comparison and SceneGen and FlashSculptor to the image-driven comparisons (Tables 2 and 5). SceneGen and FlashSculptor were cited but not evaluated in v1. The original ACDC, Gen3DSR, MIDI, and MesaTask comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 30-prompt text comparison with four GPT-rated criteria, support stability and five-second settling tests with 3 cm/30-degree thresholds, and mean-view scoring over the existing 160-view sweep. Policy evaluation adds domain randomization, 2,000 synthetic trajectories per task, and simulation-versus-reality testing. The original best-view benchmark and user-study protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds quantitative support and dynamic-settling analyses, tests sensitivity to best-view versus mean-view aggregation, and expands editing and transfer case studies. The DRO/TSA ablations are retained unchanged. Conversely, v1's efficiency analysis and dedicated cartoon reconstruction case study are removed.

E5.justification: v4 newly reports 50 evaluation trials per task in each domain for its policy-transfer success rates (Section 4.4). This supplies repetition counts for the new experiment, but neither version reports confidence intervals, variability across training seeds, or formal significance tests. User-study aggregation remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The original image-comparison, user-study, and ablation values are unchanged. New results include text-comparison average ratings of 6.27 versus MesaTask's 4.12 and Holodeck-table's 4.08, 100% support stability and 92.13% settling stability, and simulation/real policy success rates of 98/84%, 92/80%, and 90/68%. Mean-view results are also added, while the approximately 32-minute runtime result is removed. These are additional or removed findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The scene parameterization, three DRO loss terms, and RMA scoring mathematics are equivalent across versions. Combining and renumbering equations does not change their substance. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs; the added stability criteria serve as experimental evaluation procedures.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims high-quality, interactive tabletop scene generation, with manipulation learning presented as an application. v4 makes automated manipulation-data synthesis and zero-shot real-to-sim-to-real policy transfer central contributions in its title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The original scene-quality and alignment contributions remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds focused explanations for Holodeck-table's collision-versus-realism tradeoff, the larger stacking transfer gap through friction/contact/release errors, and TSA's boundary and support priors. The central interpretations of DRO/TSA effectiveness and best-view bias are retained. The limitation concerning more complex support structures also existed in v1.

D1.justification: v4 discloses the retained test set's 74-synthetic/4-real composition and category counts, identifies the motion planner and transfer robot, and illustrates synchronized camera and joint-state data. However, it removes v1's RTX 4090 hardware specification, stage runtimes, and parallelization details. The explicit source-code-release promise is omitted, although the project-page link remains; neither PDF establishes an actual release. Core hyperparameters and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from broad scene synthesis and tabletop datasets toward robotic data collection, digital twins, and real-to-sim-to-real learning. v4 adds discussion and citations including RT-1, Octo, Re3Sim, ROSE, RoboTwin 2.0, and pi0.5, while removing the dedicated tabletop-dataset discussion and references such as TO-Scene and LVDiffusor. This substantially changes the work's research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around manipulation-data synthesis. Method subsections are consolidated, Extensions becomes Data Engine Demonstrations, and the appendix is reorganized into qualitative results, video demonstrations, and experimental details. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: v4 changes the predominantly two-column presentation to a single-column layout, redraws the teaser and pipeline, restructures qualitative comparisons, and adds tables and robot/data illustrations. The original scene gallery moves to the appendix, while existing DRO and TSA illustrations are merged into composite figures. Survey screenshots and prompt images are retained despite relocation.

improvement.justification: v1 supported manipulation applicability mainly through scene metrics and qualitative simulated demonstrations. v4 substantially strengthens that evidence with physical-stability tests and policy learning followed by real-robot evaluation (Figure 6 and Table 5). Additional baselines, quantitative text comparisons, and mean-view analysis address meaningful evaluation gaps. Runtime documentation is lost, and transfer evidence remains limited to three tasks in one scene without uncertainty estimates, but the new validation substantially improves support for the paper's practical utility.
